- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for volatility or reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 3–8% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.50 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 3–5 day average of prior 10–15 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for days 1–7.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often exhibits high variance; use 10-day rolling mean as baseline for correction.
- When true outcome shows rapid decline after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; apply downward bias correction of 3–7% for 3–5 periods post-peak.
